\subsection{Secondary-Output Load and Thermal Tests}

The electronic load was connected directly to the V2 secondary output.
At approximately \SI{240}{\volt} AC and \SI{50}{\hertz}, the measured
output power increased from \SI{48.7}{\watt} to \SI{137.1}{\watt} as the
load current rose from \SI{1.86}{\ampere} to \SI{10.01}{\ampere}. Over
these points the output voltage fell from \SI{26.14}{\volt} to
\SI{13.69}{\volt}, as shown in Table~\ref{tab:v2-secondary-load} and
Figure~\ref{fig:v2-secondary-load-performance}.

The thermal images in Figure~\ref{fig:v2-secondary-load-thermal} show
higher input-bridge region temperatures at the lower-power points and
increasing secondary-region temperatures as loading increased. The
input-bridge region maximum peaked at \SI{83.9}{\celsius}, while the
secondary region reached \SI{98.3}{\celsius} at the highest load point.
None of the points reached thermal equilibrium. Diode selection and the
associated design require further work, followed by temperature tests at
fixed loads to establish sustained operation.
